email.subject: Put that 10% off to good use!

review.raw_markdown:
## 2. Business Impact Score

**5 / 10**

---

## 3. What's Working

- **Coupon code is front and center.** The 10% off offer and code (`EC1P4IRPVS`) appear immediately below the header — minimal friction to redeem.
- **Hero headline is benefit-led.** "Here's to Putting Your Best Foot Forward" is warmer than a generic sale header, though it's a well-worn shoe-pun.
- **Loyalty upsell is present.** The "Being Shoe Obsessed Has Its Perks" block converts the discount hook into a membership pitch — smart sequencing.
- **Utility section at the bottom** (Shopping Made Easy / pickup options) adds practical value without crowding the main message.

---

## 4. What's Weak

- **No product photography in the body.** The hero image shows a lifestyle/fashion shot but zero actual shoes are visible in the product grid — for a footwear retailer, this is a significant miss. Shoppers can't click what they can't see.
- **Bullet copy is generic.** "Just-dropped styles from top brands," "Can't-miss deals," and "Need-to-know trends" are boilerplate. No brand names, no specific product categories, no prices — nothing anchors urgency.
- **Single CTA until the loyalty section.** One "Shop Now" button is thin for an email this length. No category tiles (Women's, Men's, Sandals, etc.) means the email dumps everything onto one click.
- **Preview text is wasted.** "+ Check out what's NEW…" followed by a long string of invisible padding characters is visible in some clients and signals low effort. The spacer characters are functioning but conspicuous.
- **Expiry text is unreadable at render size.** The fine print beneath the coupon code appears too small and low-contrast to drive urgency effectively.
- **Loyalty CTA conflict.** "Join for Free" and "Learn More" side-by-side creates a decision fork — shoppers who already have the app are ignored, and new shoppers are given two choices where one should do.

---

## 5. Recommendations

1. **Add product tiles above the fold.** 4–6 shoe thumbnails (new arrivals or bestsellers) with prices give recipients something to react to immediately.
2. **Replace generic bullets with specifics.** Name 1–2 brands in the "just-dropped" copy. "New from Nike, Steve Madden + more" outperforms "styles from top brands" every time.
3. **Add category CTAs.** Women's / Men's / Sandals / Sneakers buttons break up the single Shop Now and let recipients self-segment.
4. **Fix the expiry copy.** Make the coupon expiry date large and prominent — urgency is your sharpest conversion lever.
5. **Clean up the preview.** Replace "+ Check out what's NEW…" + spacers with a genuine second hook: "New Nike & Steve Madden just dropped — shop with your 10% off."
6. **Collapse the loyalty double-CTA.** Use a single "Join Free & Earn Perks" button. Reserve "Learn More" for a text link below.

---

## 6. Bottom Line

This email activates an existing coupon and nudges loyalty enrollment — but it squanders its biggest asset (the discount) by not pairing it with product imagery or category urgency. A shopper who opens this leaves knowing they have 10% off but has seen nothing they want to spend it on. Add shoes to the shoe email.

---

## 7. Subject Line Analysis

- **Subject:** `Put that 10% off to good use!`
- **Length:** 30 characters
- **Scores (1-10):** Clarity `7`, Curiosity `4`, Personalization `3`, Urgency `5`, Specificity `5`
- **Strengths:**
  - Short and direct — no ambiguity about the offer type
  - Conversational tone fits DSW's brand register
- **Weaknesses:**
  - "Put it to good use" is passive and consumer-burdening — implies effort, not reward
  - No time signal, no category hook; subject and preview together deliver almost identical information
- **Alt A:** `Your 10% off expires soon — new Nike, Steve Madden + more are in`
- **Alt B:** `New drops just landed. Your 10% off is waiting.`

---

## 8. Evidence

**Overall purpose:** Retention/activation email reminding a subscriber of a pending 10% discount while cross-selling new arrivals and DSW's loyalty program.

**Hero / primary value proposition:** 10% off in stores and online with a visible promo code (`EC1P4IRPVS`). Expiry date is present but rendered at an unreadably small size. The hero image is lifestyle-focused (colorful fashion/athletic aesthetic) but shows no product.

**Membership / benefits section:** "Being Shoe Obsessed Has Its Perks" block is present mid-email with a free shipping callout and two CTAs ("Join for Free" / "Learn More"). The connection between the 10% coupon and loyalty enrollment is implied but not explicitly stated (e.g., "Join and keep getting 10% off").

**Product discoverability / recommendation modules:** None visible. No product tiles, no category grid, no featured SKUs. The body copy lists categories in text bullets only.

**Utility / secondary modules:** A "Shopping Made Easy" icon strip at the bottom appears to highlight in-store, curbside, or pickup options — appropriate utility content.

**Bugs / friction / clarity issues:**
- The coupon expiry fine print is too small to read clearly in the render.
- No visible product imagery anywhere in the main body — a notable structural gap for a shoe retailer.
- Preview text padding characters are likely visible in certain inbox clients.

---

## Technical Audit

## Technical Audit — DSW "Put that 10% off to good use!"

---

### 1. Technical Summary

The email is built on Braze with a standard XHTML 1.0 Transitional skeleton and includes dark mode + Outlook app overrides. Several malformed HTML attributes and CSS errors are present that could degrade rendering across clients; the HTML source is truncated, limiting full assessment of links, merge tokens, and compliance elements.

---

### 2. Link & Tracking Issues

**Cannot fully assess** — the provided HTML is truncated before any `<a>` tags or CTA buttons appear. The following is observable from the `<head>`:

- Font assets are served from `braze-images.com` (Braze CDN). No redirect or tracking wrapper observed on these, which is expected for font files. No concern here.
- Full UTM and click-tracking review requires the complete source.

---

### 3. Rendering & Accessibility

**Issue — Missing `http-equiv` on two `<meta>` tags:**
```html
<!-- BROKEN — no http-equiv attribute -->
<meta content="text/html; charset=utf-8" />
<meta content="IE=Edge" />

<!-- CORRECT form -->
<meta http-equiv="Content-Type" content="text/html; charset=utf-8" />
<meta http-equiv="X-UA-Compatible" content="IE=Edge" />
```
Without `http-equiv`, both tags are inert. The charset declaration will not be honored by IE/Outlook rendering engine; the IE=Edge compatibility flag will not fire.

**Issue — Capitalized `Src:` in all four `@font-face` blocks:**
```css
@font-face {
  font-family: 'Futura_PT_Regular';
  Src: url("https://braze-images.com/...") format('woff');  /* invalid */
}
```
CSS property names are case-sensitive in some parsers. `Src:` is not a recognized property; `src:` is. Web font loading will silently fail in strict parsers (notably some versions of Outlook on Mac and older WebKit). All four `@font-face` declarations share this defect.

**Issue — Conflicting `text-size-adjust` values in the same rule:**
```css
* {
  -webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%;
  -ms-text-size-adjust: 100%;
  -ms-text-size-adjust: none;   /* duplicate, overrides 100% for IE */
  text-size-adjust: none;       /* overrides the vendor-prefixed 100% intent */
}
```
`text-size-adjust: none` disables resize behavior entirely on standard-compliant browsers while the prefixed declarations set it to `100%`. This inconsistency can cause text to render at unexpected sizes on mobile, particularly in Samsung Internet and Firefox Android.

**Issue — Truncated `!important` in mobile stylesheet:**
```css
@media only screen and (max-width: 480px) {
  .stack-column { display: block !important; width: 100% !importan… }
```
If this truncation exists in the delivered HTML (not just the audit excerpt), the `width: 100%` rule is an invalid declaration and the mobile stacked-column layout will break on narrow viewports.

**Issue — Invalid CSS property in `:root` dark mode block:**
```css
:root {
  color-scheme: light dark;
  supported-color-schemes: light dark;  /* not a valid CSS property */
}
```
`supported-color-schemes` is only valid as a `<meta>` tag attribute (which is correctly present in `<head>`). Inside a CSS `:root` block it is ignored by all clients. Not harmful, but adds dead code.

---

### 4. Personalization & Merge Tokens

**Cannot fully assess** — HTML source is truncated before body content. No merge tokens (e.g., `{{first_name}}`, Braze Liquid tags) are visible in the provided excerpt. Review of the complete source is required to confirm all tokens have fallback values set.

---

### 5. Compliance (CAN-SPAM, Unsubscribe, Authentication Headers)

**Cannot fully assess** — Unsubscribe link, physical mailing address, and List-Unsubscribe header are not present in the truncated `<head>` excerpt (as expected — these appear in footer and envelope headers). Full source and raw message headers are required to confirm:

- `List-Unsubscribe` and `List-Unsubscribe-Post` headers (one-click unsubscribe per RFC 8058 / Google/Yahoo sender requirements)
- Physical postal address in footer
- SPF/DKIM pass on `e.dsw.com` sending domain

**Observable:** Sending domain is `e.dsw.com` (ESP subdomain), which is standard for Braze deployments. DKIM alignment requires `d=` tag on the `e.dsw.com` domain or a parent domain match.

---

### 6. Email-to-Site Continuity (UTM Params, Landing Page Alignment)

**Cannot assess** — no anchor tags visible in truncated source. Requires full HTML to audit UTM parameters on CTA links, consistency of `utm_campaign` values, and landing page alignment with offer messaging.

---

### 7. Recommendations

| Priority | Item | Action |
|---|---|---|
| High | Missing `http-equiv` on charset and IE-Edge meta tags | Add `http-equiv="Content-Type"` and `http-equiv="X-UA-Compatible"` |
| High | `Src:` → `src:` in all four `@font-face` blocks | Lowercase the property name; verify font fallback stack renders correctly without web fonts |
| Medium | `text-size-adjust: none` conflict | Resolve to a single value; `100%` is the safer choice for email contexts |
| Medium | Truncated `width: 100% !importan…` | Confirm this is a source-excerpt artifact; fix if present in live send |
| Low | Dead `:root { supported-color-schemes }` CSS property | Remove — it does nothing and the correct `<meta>` tag is already present |
| Audit-blocked | Links, UTMs, merge tokens, compliance footer | Re-run audit against complete untruncated HTML source |
